quote: On the Equations z^m = F(x, y) and Ax^p + By^q = Cz^r - Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society, 1995
note: The Darmon-Granville theorem of 1995 proved unconditionally that for fixed (p, q, r) with 1/p + 1/q + 1/r < 1, there are only finitely many primitive solutions to the generalized Fermat equation. This foundational result led to the formulation of what is now known as the Fermat-Catalan conjecture.
